meta.name: mnemos-longmemeval-style-40
meta.protocol: LongMemEval-style ability taxonomy (Wu et al., arXiv:2410.10813) applied to an in-house 40-question set. NOT score-comparable with published LongMemEval numbers.
meta.persona: Ola — cognitive-science master student and freelance UI designer; moves Kraków to Wrocław, changes job, design tool, teaching slot, relationship status and coffee habit, adopts a cat named after a star.
meta.clockNote: Memory dates are day offsets from an injected now. This file uses nowIso; the runner re-anchors the vault on the live clock so the 21-day decay half-life behaves the same whenever the benchmark is run.
meta.oracle: lowercased substring mustAll / mustAny / mustNot over the answer text; abstention graded by the I-dont-remember pattern; fromAge questions are graded on the memory age the prompt shows.

memories.text: Ola lived her whole childhood in Gdańsk near the Shipyard Square and her family is still there.
Her mother Aneta lives in the Gdańsk flat and gardens at the weekend.
Ola lived in Kraków after moving from Gdańsk for a master of cognitive science at Jagiellonian University.
Ola lives in Kraków, in a shared flat on Floreńska street with two lab roommates.
Her younger brother Kuba studies dentistry in Lublin and calls every Sunday evening.
Mateusz, her friend since Gdańsk, works as a live sound engineer.
Her master thesis studies cognitive load in navigation apps for elderly drivers.
Her supervisor Dr. Ewa Zielińska expects a written update every Friday.
Ola drafts every thesis chapter in Polish and translates the abstract into English last.
The machine Ola wrote her thesis on was the university Windows desktop, because it ran the eye tracking software.
Ola's job was a research internship at the cognitive science lab, coding eye tracking pilots in Python.
Ola set her thesis submission deadline for May.
Ola's birthday is 14 March.
Ola's coffee habit in Kraków was three flat whites a day, and she could not start work without them.
Ola plays a little acoustic guitar, only three chords, mostly at parties.
She walks along the Oława river after work to calm down; twenty minutes clears her head.
Reading notes after midnight wrecks her writing block and she sleeps badly.
The best writing of the day happens between 6 and 9, so Ola protects that morning block.
Ola took her first freelance client, a bike rental startup in Kazimierz, while still a student.
Ola prefers Figma for all her design work and calls it the only design tool she trusts.
Freelance client Nordwind Books still owes an invoice of 2,400 PLN for a cover redesign.
Client Zielone Podróże paid a 3,800 PLN invoice for a booking flow redesign.
Client Astro Collective sent an invoice for a brand refresh quote of 5,000 PLN.
Ola switched her design work to Penpot and calls it the design tool she trusts, because she can self host it.
She writes design tokens in a code editor instead of a separate design app.
Ola bought a used Fujifilm X-T30 camera to photograph the city at night.
She is saving 3,000 PLN for a proper 35mm lens.
Ola's coffee now is a V60 filter brewed at home, two cups at most.
Ola lives in Wrocław now, alone in a one bedroom flat on Powstańców Śląskich; she moved there in September.
Ola joined a bouldering gym near her old flat and climbed twice a week.
A grey stray cat kept appearing by the bakery door on Kalwaryjska and Ola left food out for the cat.
Ola adopted the grey stray cat and named her Vega, after the star in the Lyra constellation.
Vega chews cable sleeves, so Ola hides her laptop charger before working on the train.
Ola says her relationship status is single, with no time for dating while the thesis runs.
Ola updated her relationship status: she is with Piotr, a paramedic she met at the bouldering gym.
Vega passed her first vet check and needs a dental cleaning next spring.
Ola teaches an Intro to UX workshop on Wednesdays, an evening class at a coding school in Kraków.
She keeps cherry tomatoes and basil in pots on the balcony.
Her neighbour Pan Henryk has an old beagle called Bursztynek.
Ola says the Kraków winters were the worst part of living there.
She ran six kilometres along the Vistula every Sunday morning.
Ola ran her first half marathon in Wrocław in 2 hours 14 minutes.
Ola's new job is full time product designer at Skyward, an aviation analytics startup.
Her team at Skyward is two designers and a research lead named Tomasz.
She commutes by train and writes on the ride using only the laptop battery.
Her thesis defence is booked for 10 December in the psychology building.
The Wrocław landlord raised the rent, so she looks for a new flat near the office.
The machine Ola writes her thesis on is a used MacBook Air with Apple silicon.
She joined a Thursday cycling club in Wrocław and stopped the Sunday runs of Kraków.
After the move Ola teaches a Saturday design class in Wrocław, a morning workshop for juniors.
Ola's thesis submission deadline is now 18 November, after the original date slipped.
Ola's older sister Kaja is a physiotherapist in Poznań and expects her first baby in February.
She will be a bridesmaid at her cousin's wedding in Zakopane next June.
Ola plans a small birthday dinner on 14 March with Piotr and Mateusz.
Vega sleeps on the windowsill above the bike path and watches the crows.
She started painting small gouache studies of the night sky at the weekend.
Ola bought a standing desk converter and works standing when her back aches.
Piotr cooks the Easter dinner at her mother's flat in Gdańsk this year.
She is answering design messages late at night again, which wrecks her morning writing block.
